correctness.rationale: Differentiation of the normalized unit-state perturbation gives the radial quadratic form involving uG'(u)+u²G''(u) and the normalization term. Analytic Fourier orthogonality removes mixed n coefficients. Expressing arbitrary C2 convex G as affine plus integral of hinges and integrating by parts proves H_{n+1}(a)-H_n(a)= -C_n a^(beta-1)(1-a)^n(1+na)/[beta(n+1)] at a=s^(1/beta); positivity of G'' on a nonempty interval makes all gaps strictly positive. The n=1 coefficient vanishes by invariance, and dominated convergence gives finite lambda_infty. Independently checked 63 exact rational degree gaps for 3 beta values, 3 powers and 7 consecutive degrees. Global stability beyond quadratic order is NOT asserted.

value.rationale: The exact local spectral Hessian quantifies a known optimality theorem rather than repeating it, simultaneously for every non-affine convex observable. The symmetry kernel and the universal degree-two least-stable direction identify a sharp infinitesimal stability benchmark relevant to coherent-state concentration.

final_claim: For every beta>1 and every non-affine C2 convex G on [0,1] with G(0)=0, the Hessian at any weighted Bergman coherent state diagonalizes with phase/degree-one symmetry zero directions; the positive eigenvalues for degrees n>=2 are strictly ordered, degree two uniquely least stable, and the exact mode-gap and lambda2 integrals hold.
limitations: Infinitesimal pure-state weighted analytic disk perturbations, beta>1 and G C2 convex; no globally sharp nonlinear coefficient, mixed-state result or higher-dimensional extension.
